The diaphragm is a dome: on axial slices near its apex, the uppermost part of the liver (or of the spleen on the left) appears as a round image of soft tissue surrounded by lung, and may look like a mass. It is enough to follow it on the subsequent slices: it widens and continues with the organ below the diaphragm. Coronal and sagittal reformats remove any doubt.
This CT comes from the LIDC-IDRI collection: none of the 4 thoracic radiologists marked nodules or other lesions.
